fine_trace.note: The type string of the second part's 'timecode' attribute ('int' instead of 'timecode') is read directly from the attacker-controlled file header, so the attribute is registered with a non-timecode built-in type.

Because the declared type is 'int', the attribute is mapped to EXR_ATTR_INT, a POD type stored in-place in the exr_attribute_t union, so the union member used later for timecode data is never initialized as a pointer.
attr_init zeroes the union (POD int member) for the 'timecode'-named attribute of type EXR_ATTR_INT; the 8 bytes that would be interpreted as the timecode pointer are all zero.

fine_trace.code: case EXR_ATTR_INT: rv = extract_attr_32bit (ctxt, scratch, &(nattr->i), name, type, attrsz, 1);
fine_trace.note: The 4-byte integer payload (value 0 in the crafted file) is copied into the POD union member, leaving the union bytes that the validation code will later read as a timecode pointer equal to NULL.

fine_trace.code: if (rval == EXR_ERR_SUCCESS) rval = add_to_list (ctxt, list, nattr, name);
fine_trace.note: The mis-typed 'timecode' attribute (type EXR_ATTR_INT, POD zero value) is appended to part 1's attribute list under the name 'timecode', where it will be found by name during shared-attribute validation.

fine_trace.code: rv = internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs (ctxt, ctxt->parts[0], curp, p, mismatch, &mismatchcount);
fine_trace.note: After both part headers of the multipart file are parsed, shared attributes of part 1 (curp) are validated against part 0, reaching the by-name 'timecode' comparison.
exr_get_attribute_by_name returns part 1's attribute solely by matching the name 'timecode'; the returned EXR_ATTR_INT attribute is accepted without checking its type.

Root cause: the code only tests that both parts contain an attribute named 'timecode', never verifying cattr->type is EXR_ATTR_TIMECODE before accessing the union through cattr->timecode; the safety condition that should have held is cattr->type == EXR_ATTR_TIMECODE.

Sink: memcmp dereferences cattr->timecode, which is NULL (the zeroed POD union of the EXR_ATTR_INT attribute read through the timecode pointer member), causing an invalid 8-byte read at address 0x0 and a segmentation fault.
